title: China’s Asian Affairs Reshuffle
author: Sumiya Chuluunbaatar
text:
Mongolian President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa receives then-Chinese Ambassador Shen Minjuan and awards her the Order of the Polar State, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, July 22, 2026.
Credit: Office of the President of Mongolia
On July 21, President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa awarded Shen Minjuan, China’s ambassador to the country since 2023, Mongolia’s Order of the Polar Star (Altan Gerege), the country’s highest state honor for foreign nationals. Barely a week later, on July 29, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) updated its official organizational roster: Shen had taken office as director-general of the Department of Asian Affairs, succeeding Liu Jinsong. The speed of the promotion was striking. So was its symbolism. For Mongolian policymakers and analysts who observed Shen’s nearly three-year tenure up close, her elevation to one of the most influential operational posts in Chinese foreign policy is more than a routine bureaucratic rotation. It is the clearest signal yet that Beijing is recalibrating its approach to its immediate periphery – moving away from the overtly assertive style that defined much of the past half-decade toward a more calibrated, geoeconomics-driven model.[...]
